item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract because it exposes the exact required Upload signature and reuses FilesOption. Neither patch is merge-ready: both add forbidden association machinery, bypass FilesService.Add, alter retry internals, and omit source-reader failure coverage.","reasons":["B implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) exactly; A instead introduces incompatible AddFileOption machinery.","A duplicates the repository’s existing option pattern and adds numerous association-specific APIs, creating substantially more unauthorized public surface.","B has stronger direct Upload coverage for multipart encoding, validation, and retry, although its retry test uses strings.Reader rather than a genuinely non-replayable stream.","Both duplicate Add’s request/response logic by calling Raw.Do directly, violating the requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add."],"risks_a":["makeBodyReplayable globally buffers every non-replayable Raw.Do body, an explicitly out-of-scope retry refactor with potentially large memory impact.","makeBodyReplayable silently ignores io.ReadAll failures after consuming part of the source, allowing a truncated or otherwise corrupted request to proceed.","Upload has the wrong option type and adds forbidden association APIs and multipart-field machinery without testing source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["WithFilesFormFields adds association fields expressly forbidden by the contract and changes FilesOption behavior across methods.","enableBodyReplay changes global Raw.Do ownership and closing semantics and reuses the same seeker instance for every body replay.","Upload does not call FilesService.Add, and tests omit explicit source-reader failure propagation and a genuinely streamed-content retry case."]}
